schmecken + dative: dir.

English: Can you lend **me** your bike? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: leihen: to lend; the one who gets it is in the dative.

English: **There are** a lot of restaurants here.
note — the bold part is what the card te: es gibt stays singular, even for many things.
Gibt es…? asks whether something is available.
gibt es + accusative: eine Toilette.
es gibt ein Problem: there's a problem.
hier first, the verb second: gibt es.
A pronoun goes before a noun: ihm (dative), then den Apfel.
der Apfel → ihn. An accusative pronoun goes before the dative noun.
Two pronouns: the accusative first, then the dative.
Two nouns: the dative before the accusative.

English: Can you show **me** the way? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: mir before den Weg: the pronoun first.
uns (dative pronoun) before die Frage (accusative noun).
Dative noun first, then the accusative noun: unserer Oma Blumen.
schenken: to give as a present. Dative noun, then accusative noun.
das Buch → es. The pronoun jumps ahead of the dative noun.
dir before den Schlüssel: pronoun before noun.

English: I'll bring **it to you**. (the key; one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Schlüssel → ihn. Two pronouns: accusative, then dative.

English: The photos? I'll show **them to you**. (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: die Fotos → sie (accusative), then dir.

English: Can you explain **it to me**? (the question; one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: die Frage → sie, then mir, then the infinitive.
